# Character armoring lane — production topology, semantic coverage, and one-draw anatomy hiding

This is the production contract for turning generated character/gear candidates into runtime-ready GalaQuest assets. It complements [gear.md](gear.md): that file owns mounting/fit; this file owns topology and body coverage.

## 1. Generated bytes are source art, not shipping art

A provider `SUCCEEDED` result is a **source/candidate**. Run the zero-dependency intake report before treating it as production material:

```bash
node tools/assets/glb-intake-report.mjs <candidate.glb> [...]
```

Record at least bytes, triangles, vertices, primitives/draws, skin/joint count, animations, and suspicious material defaults. Do not normalize a provider's polygon count into a new game budget just because the model looks good in its thumbnail.

For deforming characters, prefer this production order when the provider supports it:

**reference/T-pose → generate → silhouette review → remesh to the intended runtime topology → rig the remeshed winner → built-in walk/run → Studio → running game**

Rigging a ~300k-face source and only later discovering that the game needs a tiny fraction of that topology creates avoidable deformation and rework risk. Existing proof specimens may have taken that route; do not make it the mass-production default.

For rigid gear:

**reference → generate → silhouette review → remesh/decimate → material normalization → fit/mount → Studio → running game**

Use the current Hero/equipped-character contract to allocate a triangle budget to the whole visible loadout. A helmet, two shoulders, weapon, and shield all consume real budget. Do not invent a generous per-item budget in isolation.

## 2. Do not split anatomy into permanent render meshes just to hide it

The current runtime Hero body is one skinned primitive. Hair and ears are not independent runtime nodes that can simply be toggled. The equipped-character contract is also intentionally draw-call constrained, so turning `hair`, `leftEar`, `rightEar`, torso pieces, and limbs into extra always-managed render meshes is not the default architecture.

GalaQuest instead uses **semantic anatomy coverage** while preserving a one-draw body:

- gear declares the anatomy it covers, e.g. a full helm can declare `hair` + `ears`;
- the body carries semantic triangle/corner regions;
- the runtime selects a cached index-buffer variant that omits covered triangles while reusing the original position/UV/skin buffers;
- the body remains one mesh/primitive/draw;
- removing the gear restores the original geometry exactly.

The runtime core lives in `public/src/character/anatomyOcclusion.js`. It fails closed if an asset is untagged or a triangle crosses semantic regions rather than guessing from world-space bounds.

## 3. Author semantic regions on face corners, not extra materials

The preferred shipping representation is a custom mesh attribute named `_GQ_REGION`, authored on Blender **face corners** so each triangle has one unambiguous semantic code. Blender's glTF exporter exports mesh attributes whose names begin with `_`, and the vendored three.js loader exposes that attribute to GalaQuest as `_gq_region`.

Current semantic vocabulary starts narrow on purpose:

- `core`
- `hair`
- `ears`
- `beard`
- `torso`
- `upper-arms`
- `lower-arms`
- `hands`
- `hips-legs`
- `feet`

Do **not** tag every microscopic body feature because a taxonomy exists. Start with the regions real gear needs and expand only when another accepted equipment type proves the need.

For the current Dawnwarden helmet, the intended rule is:

**hide `hair` + `ears`; preserve face, eyes, and brows.**

Headgear type matters. A later hat may keep ears/beard and use a helmet-compatible under-hair fall; a full helm can hide much more. `head slot occupied` is not a sufficient coverage rule.

## 4. Supervised semantic authoring is currently mandatory

Do not ship a mask inferred only from texture colour, bounding boxes, or connected-component guesses. PR #26 R&D on the actual Hero showed why: hair/ears are integrated into the head topology and facial features such as brows are painted into that same textured surface. Simple colour/spatial inference can look plausible at one angle while deleting face triangles at another.

Automation may **propose** region masks. Acceptance still requires fixed-angle overlays and the actual equip/unequip result in Character Studio. A production tag pass must prove:

- hair is gone where the helmet needs clearance;
- ears are gone when the headgear class requires it;
- eyes/brows/face remain intact;
- no exposed scalp/face holes appear outside the helmet coverage;
- removing the helmet restores the untouched Hero;
- idle/walk/run/attack do not reintroduce clipping.

This is a one-time cost per base character topology, not per armor asset. Once a Hero/body is semantically tagged, many equipment pieces can reuse those coverage atoms.

## 5. Mass-production gate

No generated character or armor candidate is promoted from `candidates/` until all applicable gates pass:

1. intake report recorded;
2. topology reduced to a budget justified by the actual visible loadout;
3. material defaults normalized/re-exported;
4. rigid vs deforming attachment strategy chosen correctly;
5. coverage metadata declared where the item replaces/occludes anatomy;
6. Studio front/side/back/3Q plus relevant animation checks pass;
7. gameplay-scale portrait/landscape pixels still read as the intended fantasy;
8. shipping tests and payload/draw budgets remain green.

Optimize for the pixels a child actually sees. Preserve silhouette and fit before preserving invisible provider detail.
